french.note: Commonly given as 50-60. A web check found the giberne itself held only 30-35; the rest was carried in the pack. Unverified.

british.note: Sixty-round pouch (confirmed by secondary web pages, search snippet).

french_massed.note: Commonly given as 50-60. A web check found the giberne itself held only 30-35; the rest was carried in the pack. Unverified.

roundshot.note: Trail chest plus one caisson with the battery. Further caissons in the park are not modelled. Unverified.

canister.note: About a fifth to a quarter of the ready ammunition. Unverified.

roundshot.note: Gribeauval 12-pdr: 9 in the trail chest and 48 in one caisson (Wikipedia, Canon de 12 Gribeauval; search snippet).

firstVolleyBonus.note: A battalion's first volley was loaded at leisure and fired from clean barrels (Muir and Nosworthy, from memory). The size of the advantage is a guess.

foulingRounds.note: Volleys after which barrels are fully fouled and flints worn. Commonly put at 20-30.

foulingSlowdown.note: Reload time is multiplied by 1 + this x fouling: 2 rounds a minute falls to 1.3. Consistent with '2-3 at first, 1-2 sustained'.

foulingMisfire.note: Hits are multiplied by 1 - this x fouling. A clean flintlock already misfired about one round in six (secondary: Wikipedia and 1834 British trials, search snippet); that is inside the battlefield factor.

resupplyTime.note: A battalion with no formed enemy within resupplyDistance for this long is refilled from its reserve cartridges.

resupplyFraction.note: Brought up to at least this share of a full load.

maxResupplies.note: The battalion's own reserve, once. Guns are not resupplied.
